[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.31.1[/b][/size]

0.31.0 shipped three faults. All three were found by being asked the right questions, not by any
automated check.

[b]The horde never reacted[/b]

You could be Plumjum Khan's Champion and his betrayer at the same time, and he never found out.
Handing his east cave to a rival stood down *Butu's* goblins and nothing else — the Warrens, the
Mongol Camp, the Khan, Rakeb and every piece of Horde-gated dialogue carried on as though nothing had
happened.

The switch for it already existed: [i]Make Goblins Hostile Relay[/i] sits in [b]fourteen[/b] goblin maps and
vanilla throws it over a hundred times. Siding with the heir now throws it in [b]the Goblin Warrens and
the Mongol Camp[/b] — his two real settlements. The outlying villages are deliberately left alone,
because the horde is large and news travels slowly.

[b]The errand could dead-end[/b]

[i]Butu Khan's Poems[/i] could become impossible to finish, and the ordering made that likely rather than
unlikely: Weng Choi's rare-books job is an act 1 errand, and the heir does not exist until after
Montserrat.

The turn-in removes the book, Weng Choi's shop stocks [b]no books at all[/b], and the Goblin Warrens copy
is the only one in the game. An earlier note claimed you could buy it back. You cannot.

Vanilla had already drawn the distinction the scene needed — the quest is called *Complete Weng Choi's
Book Collection* and calls him [b]"an avid collector of unique tomes."[/b] So giving a dead Khan's poems
to a collector is not the same act as selling them by weight, and the heir cares which:

| | |
|---|---|
| you kept the book | he takes it in both hands and does not open it. Still the best of the three |
| you gave it to the collector | *"A human who keeps words he cannot eat… Then Butu is read in a city that never heard of him, which is further than Plumjum has ever carried anything."* |
| you sold it | he puts his hand out and [b]takes back the 250 you were paid[/b]. *"I did not pick the number. A human did, and you took it."* |

Three ways to close it now, and no dead end. The insult in the third is the price, not a refusal.

[b]And the reward was nothing[/b]

Siding with the heir paid experience and a cave whose hidden treasure is [b]one Potion[/b], against
losing your goblin standing, two settlements and Grumdjum as a late-game companion. It was strictly
worse than killing him, which is backwards.

The standing now [b]swaps[/b] instead of vanishing — and it is tiered, because Hrargrub gains more by
taking the Khan's Champion than by taking a chum:

| what you gave up | what you become | what it grants |
|---|---|---|
| never joined | [b]Goblin Traitor - Foe[/b] | melee +10 |
| Chum or Blooded | [b]Goblin Traitor - Bad Blood[/b] | melee +20, crushing resistance +15 |
| Champion | [b]Goblin Traitor - Fallen Champion[/b] | melee +35, crushing +30, slashing +20, carry +20 |

The horde pays in sneaking and poison resistance because it is Mongol-trained. Butu's line were never
trained by anyone and only ever had what they killed, so they pay in melee and in not going down. The
middle tier is deliberately [b]not[/b] a straight upgrade — a Chum gives up poison resistance and carry
weight entirely.

The title perk stays on your sheet alongside the old one, because nothing in the engine can take a
perk off. That seems right. You *were* his Champion.

[i]*TITLE PERK: You handed the Khan's east rock to Butu's heir. The Horde has a word for it and the[/i]
[i]word is not Champion.*[/i]

[b]A use for the deed, and two that were wrong[/b]

The [b]Silver Mine Deed[/b] is one of twelve unique items the shipped game references from nothing:
*"Legal document proscribing ownership of the Silver Mine."*

Two uses were proposed and dropped as mistimed — having Eduardo accept it instead of the silver, and
opening the mine with it. Both are act 1 problems, and the deed does not exist until after Montserrat,
so for most players they would be answers to a question already settled.

The mine route is kept anyway, because it matters more than it looks: betraying Plumjum closes the
Horde route past the mine foreman, and the deed is what reopens it. Side with the heir and you are not
locked out of the Sacred Scimitar.

And Shylocke is not time-locked. He holds Shakespeare's muse as collateral and sues Cortes over a
clause in their contract, so a mine deed is his actual trade. He also opens low, because he is
Shylocke:

| | |
|---|---|
| no haggling | [b]1200[/b] — *"Twelve hundred, and I will never visit it."* |
| Barter 40 | [b]1800[/b] — *"It pays whether you go or not."* |
| Barter 70 | [b]2500[/b] |

[i]*"Then it is mine, and the goblins in it are mine, and I shall do what I have always done with[/i]
[i]property I cannot visit. Nothing whatsoever, at a profit."*[/i]

[b]Installing[/b]

Unzip and double-click [b][i]Mod Manager.bat[/i][/b], then click the button that names the mod.

As with 0.31.0, the cave changing hands needs a save that has [b]not[/b] been into the Ravine Cave's east
half. Everything else here is dialogue and character data and applies immediately.

[b]If you play it[/b]

[b]One test matters more than the rest.[/b] As a Goblin Champion, write down your Sneak, Barter, carry
weight and poison and disease resistance. Side with Butu's heir. Read them again.

The sneak-and-poison bonuses should have come off and melee and armour gone on. If the old numbers are
[b]still there on top of the new ones[/b], then character factions in this engine accumulate rather than
replace, an assumption this release rests on is wrong, and a mechanism I deleted needs to come back.
Please report the actual numbers rather than whether it looked right — that one reading decides it.

After that: side with the heir and check the Khan and Grumdjum both stay away in Persia; confirm the
Warrens and the Mongol Camp attack you while the outlying goblin villages do not; and take the deed to
the mine foreman to see the route your betrayal closed reopen.
